subject.title: fix(clickclack): add timeouts to REST client requests

question: Should ClickClack permanently use a fixed 30-second completion deadline for every non-multipart REST operation while leaving multipart uploads unbounded?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically sound, but the threshold and request-class exception determine when existing self-hosted deployments begin failing and cannot be selected safely from tests alone.

options.title: Approve JSON-only deadline
options.body: Accept the fixed 30-second policy and multipart exception as the intended ClickClack reliability tradeoff.

options.title: Retune before merge
options.body: Choose owner-approved JSON and upload deadlines, then update the constant, comments, and focused proof accordingly.

options.title: Pause for latency evidence
options.body: Hold the PR until representative ClickClack deployment latency and ambiguous-send behavior justify a permanent threshold.

recommendation.title: Approve JSON-only deadline
recommendation.body: Accept the fixed 30-second policy and multipart exception as the intended ClickClack reliability tradeoff.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest available recent ClickClack runtime-history signal for routing the owner-policy decision.
